articles.title: Former India pacer Javagal Srinath spotted travelling in Bengaluru Metro with trolley bag: Internet praises his simplicity
articles.summary: There was no cricket ground, no television camera and no entourage. Just a former India fast bowler, a trolley bag and an ordinary ride on Bengaluru's.
articles.body: There was no cricket ground, no television camera and no entourage. Just a former India fast bowler, a trolley bag and an ordinary ride on Bengaluru's Metro.A photograph of Javagal Srinath travelling on Namma Metro has caught the attention of cricket fans online, not because of anything extraordinary happening in the frame, but because of how ordinary it looks. The former India pacer is seen travelling like any other commuter, carrying his luggage and going about his day.For a cricketer who once led India's pace attack and was one of the country's most recognisable fast bowlers, the sight has struck a chord with fans. Social media users were quick to praise Srinath's unassuming nature, with several recalling other occasions when the Karnataka cricketer has been seen away from the spotlight.From the 'Mysore Express' to a Metro commuterNicknamed the 'Mysore Express', the Karnataka-born fast bowler became one of India's most important quicks during an era when the country was still searching for a consistent pace attack. He represented India in 67 Tests and 229 ODIs.Years after his retirement, however, it is not one of his wickets or spells that has brought him back into the social media spotlight. It is a quiet moment.In the viral photograph, Srinath is dressed casually in jeans and a light-blue shirt. A trolley bag stands beside him as he travels inside the Metro. There is little to suggest that the passenger in the frame once played international cricket for India. That contrast appears to be precisely what appealed to fans.Fans react: 'This is Srinath'The photograph triggered a stream of reactions from cricket followers, many of whom described Srinath's simplicity as something they had come to associate with him. Some users said they had spotted him in Bengaluru before, moving around the city without the kind of attention or security that often surrounds former international stars.Others brought up former Karnataka teammates and contemporaries such as Rahul Dravid and Venkatesh Prasad while discussing the understated public lives of several cricketers from the state, writing: “Anil Kumble, Javagal Srinath, Rahul Dravid, and Venkatesh Prasad represented a unique era or Karnataka cricket, proving that immense sporting success can coexist with absolute humility and grace.”For many fans, the picture offered a reminder that sporting fame does not necessarily have to translate into a celebrity lifestyle.A familiar face away from the cricket fieldThis is not the first time Srinath's everyday life has attracted attention. A photograph shared by a fan in the past showed him waiting at Mysuru railway station with a bag on his back. That image too drew appreciation from people who were struck by how casually the former India star appeared to be going about his business. The Metro photograph has created a similar reaction.However, the exact date on which the Bengaluru Metro photograph was taken could not be independently verified. The image surfaced online and subsequently began circulating widely on social media.What is Srinath doing now?Srinath may have walked away from international cricket, but he did not walk away from the game. Following his playing career, he took up the role of an ICC match referee and has remained involved in international cricket in that capacity.His transition from one of India's premier fast bowlers to a match official has kept him connected to the sport, albeit from a very different position. For a generation of Indian cricket fans, though, Srinath remains the fast bowler who carried much of India's pace responsibility through the 1990s.That is perhaps why a seemingly routine Metro journey has attracted so much attention. The photograph does not show a former India star surrounded by fans or celebrating another cricketing achievement. It shows something much simpler: a man travelling through his city with a bag. And for thousands of fans watching from their screens, that simplicity has become the story.Looking for trusted parenting advice? articles.body: Shubman Gill's presence added a special touch to the jersey launch of Fazilka Falcons ahead of the Sher-E-Punjab T20 League 2026.The India captain, who will lead the Fazilka-based side, personally designed the team's jersey, while the kit was unveiled at an event in Chandigarh.The jersey launch became a family moment with Gill's father Lakhwinder Singh Gill among those present for the unveiling. The design draws inspiration from Punjab's culture, traditions and heritage while giving the team a modern identity.Fazilka Falcons owner Khushpreet Singh Aulakh said the involvement of Gill made the jersey particularly meaningful.“Today is a very special occasion for Fazilka Falcons and for everyone associated with the team. Having Shubman Gill personally design the jersey makes it even more meaningful because it brings together cricket and the rich culture of Punjab. The design reflects the pride, traditions and spirit of our state, while also giving the team a strong identity of its own,” he said.Falcons ready for inaugural campaignThe jersey was unveiled on National Sports Day, adding significance to an event celebrating sport and athletes. The Falcons will feature a combination of experienced players and young talent, with Gill leading the team in the inaugural season.“For the people of Punjab, this jersey is not just a team kit, it represents our culture, our passion for cricket and the dreams of the young players who will be taking the field. We are proud to unveil it on National Sports Day and hope the people of Punjab connect with the jersey and proudly support the Fazilka Falcons throughout the tournament,” Aulakh added.The Sher-E-Punjab T20 League will begin on August 30 and run until September 13 at the I.S. articles.title: Watch: Captain Vaibhav Sooryavanshi’s brave DRS call gets East Zone crucial wicket
articles.summary: Cricket News: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation showed remarkable composure and instinct when he took charge of East Zone du.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Vaibhav Sooryavanshi may only be 15, but the teenage sensation showed remarkable composure and instinct when he took charge of East Zone during their Duleep Trophy semifinal against Central Zone in Bengaluru on Sunday.With East Zone chasing control over the opening day’s proceedings, Sooryavanshi made a crucial leadership call in the 40th over that immediately paid off. The youngster opted for a Decision Review System (DRS) review after an appeal for a caught behind was turned down by the on-field umpire — and the decision resulted in the wicket of Aryan Juyal.The moment came when Juyal, batting on 46, pushed hard at a delivery from Mukesh Kumar outside the off stump. The East Zone players immediately went up in appeal, convinced that the batter had edged the ball behind.However, the umpire was unmoved.With some East Zone players appearing uncertain about whether to take the review, Sooryavanshi trusted his instinct and called for DRS at the last moment. The review proved the youngster right, with UltraEdge detecting a small spike as the ball passed the bat.Juyal was given out, handing East Zone a crucial breakthrough and underlining Sooryavanshi's growing maturity in his first stint as captain in senior first-class cricket.Watch:Sooryavanshi steps up after Kishan injuryThe captaincy opportunity came unexpectedly for the 15-year-old.Sooryavanshi is normally East Zone's vice-captain, but regular skipper Ishan Kishan was forced off the field after suffering a thumb injury while keeping wickets. Kumar Kushagra took over the wicketkeeping duties, while Sooryavanshi temporarily assumed leadership responsibilities.The teenager's ability to make an important decision under pressure added another layer to what has already been an eventful Duleep Trophy campaign for him.Sooryavanshi had a modest outing with the bat in East Zone's quarter-final against North East Zone, scoring just eight runs. However, he made an impact with the ball, claiming two wickets.Speaking about his bowling experience and his expanding role in the team, Sooryavanshi said he enjoys the opportunity to contribute in different ways."If you ask any batter, they always enjoy bowling. A batter always enjoys bowling and a bowler always enjoys batting equally," Sooryavanshi said in a video posted by BCCI Domestic.The youngster also revealed that Kishan had taken a chance by handing him the ball and confidently described himself as a "wicket-taker"."Opponent team's wickets weren't falling, so I was asked to bowl two or three overs. Ishan Bhaiya felt like he was taking a risk, but he didn't know that I am a wicket-taker," he added.East Zone dominate opening sessionEast Zone won the toss and opted to bowl first against Rajat Patidar's Central Zone.Their decision was rewarded almost immediately as their bowlers kept Central Zone under pressure throughout the opening session. Central were reduced to 81/3 after 32 overs, with Abhijit K Sarkar doing most of the early damage.Sarkar dismissed Aman Mokhade and Kunal Chandela before Mukesh Kumar accounted for Central captain Patidar. Mohammed Shami also kept Patidar under pressure during an intense battle.Saransh Jain returned to Central Zone's playing XI after recently making his India debut in the Colombo Test against Sri Lanka.But the key moment of the afternoon belonged to Sooryavanshi.As East Zone players debated whether to review the umpire's decision against Juyal, the teenage stand-in captain acted decisively. His call came just in time — and the tiny UltraEdge spike vindicated his judgement.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: County Championship: Durham need six balls to complete Gloucestershire win
articles.summary: Division Two leaders Durham beat Gloucestershire by 10 wickets, needing just six balls to complete a final day victory.
articles.body:
Rothesay County Championship, Division Two, Chester-le-Street (day four)

Gloucestershire 137: Aldridge 5-16 & 250: Hammond 58; Aldridge 4-47

Durham 384: Bedingham 122; Langridge 3-89 & 4-0

Durham (22 pts) defeated Gloucestershire (3 pts) by 10 wickets

Durham took just six deliveries to seal a 10-wicket victory against Gloucestershire and take another big step towards promotion back to the top flight and the Division Two title.

With second-placed Kent and third-placed Northamptonshire playing each other in this round of matches, Durham's seventh win of the season seems certain to take the leaders further ahead at the top of the table with four games to play, while Gloucestershire remain firmly rooted to the foot after suffering their ninth defeat in ten.

Needing four runs to win, Durham sent in Matty Potts and Ollie Robinson to open their second innings, and it was Potts who hit the winning boundary off some gentle off spin from Ollie Price from the final ball of the first over.

It was another convincing victory by the hosts with David Bedingham providing the batting highlight, making a superb century, his fifth in the Championship this year, with his innings of 122 taking the South African overseas batter to within 57 runs of 1,000 runs for the season.

That followed a five-wicket haul for Kasey Aldridge as Gloucestershire were bowled out for 137 on the opening day where James Bracey's battling 60 providing the main resistance.

After Durham had established a 247-run first innings lead, Aldridge struck again with 4-47 to finish with match figures of 9-63 to complete a fine display.

Brydon Carse chipped in with four important wickets and the inclusion of Carse, Ben Stokes and Matty Potts headlined the quality on show in this match to highlight the strength of the competition.

Miles Hammond made 58 as Gloucestershire's 250 took the visitors just ahead on the third evening before bad light prevented Durham hitting the four runs required until this morning.

Durham travel to Northampton while Gloucestershire return to Bristol to play Derbyshire, who they defeated by 10 wickets back in April, in the next round of matches starting on Wednesday.

articles.title: Big Blow for South Africa! Kagiso Rabada likely to miss Australia Test series with Hamstring Injury
articles.summary: Cricket News: South Africa are likely to suffer a major blow ahead of their three-match Test series against Australia, with premier fast bowler Kagiso Rabada ruled .
articles.body: South Africa are likely to suffer a major blow ahead of their three-match Test series against Australia, with premier fast bowler Kagiso Rabada ruled out after sustaining a severe Grade 3 tear in his right hamstring.The injury, picked up during Rabada’s winter conditioning programme, is expected to keep him out for up to 10 weeks, ruling him out of the high-profile series that begins in Durban on October 9.Donald confirms Rabada absenceFormer South Africa fast bowler and current Lions bowling coach Allan Donald confirmed that Rabada will miss the entire series, ending hopes of having him available for the domestic season.“He’s going to be out for all the Aussie Tests as well,” Donald was quoted as saying by South African media outlet News24 on Sunday.South Africa are scheduled to face Australia in three Tests, with the second match in Gqeberha from October 18 and the final Test in Cape Town from October 27. The series will be preceded by a three-match ODI series beginning in Durban on September 24.Proteas face pace-bowling concernsRabada’s absence leaves a significant void in the South African bowling attack. Gerald Coetzee, Corbin Bosch and youngster Kwena Maphaka are likely to shoulder greater responsibility in his absence. South Africa are also monitoring the fitness of Nandre Burger, who is recovering from a stress fracture in his back. However, there is still a chance that the left-arm pacer could recover in time to feature in the Test series.Meanwhile, Rabada has taken 340 wickets in 73 Tests and played a key role in South Africa’s victory over Australia in the 2025 World Test Championship final at Lord’s, where he finished with match figures of 9-110. He also boasts an impressive record against Australia, having claimed 58 wickets in 11 Tests at an average of 21.39.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: 417 first-class wickets, just 3 Tests: The forgotten story of Baloo Gupte, who remained in the long shadow of his elder brother Subhash Gupte
articles.summary: Cricket News: On August 30, 1934, Balkrishna Pandharinath Gupte was born into a family that would produce two accomplished leg-spinners. But while his elder brother.
articles.body: On August 30, 1934, Balkrishna Pandharinath Gupte was born into a family that would produce two accomplished leg-spinners. But while his elder brother Subhash Gupte went on to become one of the finest spinners of his generation, Baloo Gupte spent much of his cricketing life in his shadow.Baloo, as Balkrishna was known, was no ordinary cricketer. He was an orthodox leg-spinner and googly bowler who built a formidable reputation in Indian domestic cricket, taking more than 400 first-class wickets. Yet his international career never came close to matching his domestic achievements.His story is perhaps one of Indian cricket's more intriguing cases of talent that never translated into sustained success at Test level.Test debut came after brother was droppedThe irony of Baloo Gupte's international career was evident from the very beginning.Five years older, Subhash had already established himself as India's premier leg-spinner when Baloo made his Test debut. Subhash played 36 Tests for India and claimed 149 wickets, while Baloo eventually played only three Tests and finished with three wickets.Baloo's opportunity came against Pakistan at Madras during the 1960-61 series, after Subhash had been dropped. It was a difficult introduction to Test cricket. The pitch was ideal for batting, and Baloo was made to toil for 35 overs.He conceded 116 runs without taking a wicket.Rather than being the beginning of a Test career, it became an early indication of how unforgiving international cricket could be. Baloo was surprisingly recalled three years later for the home series against England, but again failed to make an impact.His third and final Test came against New Zealand at Calcutta the following season. Once again, wickets proved elusive.After three Tests, Baloo's international career was effectively over. He had taken just three wickets — one per Test — a remarkably modest return for a bowler whose domestic record told a very different story.The Duleep Trophy record that stood for almost 40 yearsIf Test cricket did not bring Baloo Gupte the recognition he deserved, domestic cricket certainly did.Representing Bombay, Bengal and Railways at different stages of his career, Gupte became one of India's leading wicket-takers. He finished his first-class career with 417 wickets, while his Ranji Trophy tally stood at 255 wickets at 23.47.Perhaps his greatest domestic performance came in the 1962-63 Duleep Trophy final.Playing for West Zone against South Zone, Gupte produced extraordinary figures of 9 for 55. At the time, it was the best innings bowling performance in Duleep Trophy history.And it remained the benchmark for almost four decades.It was only on January 25, 2001, that East Zone's Debashish Mohanty finally surpassed Gupte's record. Mohanty took 10 for 46 in 19 overs against South Zone at Agartala, becoming the first bowler in the tournament's history to claim all 10 wickets in an innings.By then, Gupte's record had stood for nearly 38 years.Subhash Gupte: the brother who became a legendThe contrast with Subhash Gupte could hardly have been greater.Subhash was widely regarded as one of the best leg-break and googly bowlers of his era. He was a big spinner of the ball, but his accuracy was just as impressive. He could flight the delivery, maintain an immaculate line and disguise his googly superbly.His Test career took off during India's tour of the West Indies in 1952-53. He claimed 50 wickets on the tour at 23.64, including 27 wickets in the Tests.He was again India's leading wicket-taker in Pakistan in 1954-55, claiming 21 wickets, before producing another remarkable campaign against New Zealand the following season. His 34 wickets at 19.67 remained an Indian record for 27 years until Bhagwat Chandrasekhar surpassed it.Subhash's finest individual Test figures came against the West Indies at Kanpur in 1958-59, when he took 9 for 102 in an innings. He finished that series with 22 wickets.His 1959 tour of England produced an astonishing 95 wickets at 26.58, although only 17 came in the five Tests.Across a first-class career stretching from 1947 to 1964, Subhash claimed 530 wickets at 23.71. His achievements included the extraordinary feat of taking all 10 wickets in an innings for Bombay against Pakistan Services and Bahawalpur CC in 1954.A career defined by the shadowSubhash and Baloo were both gifted leg-spinners. Both were prolific in domestic cricket. But history remembers them very differently.Subhash played 36 Tests and became one of India's most celebrated spinners. Baloo played three and took three wickets.Yet judging Baloo solely through his Test record would be deeply unfair.His 417 first-class wickets, 255 Ranji Trophy wickets and nine-wicket Duleep Trophy haul tell the story of a bowler who was consistently effective over a long domestic career.Baloo Gupte died on July 5, 2005, aged 70.His career remains an unusual footnote in the history of Indian cricket: a highly successful domestic bowler whose Test career began only after his world-class elder brother's exit, lasted just three matches and yielded little.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.body: Babar Azam’s prolonged Test batting slump continued at Lord’s as the Pakistan captain fell for just 6 runs in the second innings against England.Chasing a daunting 389-run target, Pakistan suffered another early setback when Jofra Archer dismissed Babar, who failed to make an impact with the bat once again. The dismissal added to a difficult period for the former Pakistan captain, who has not scored a Test century since December 2022 despite coming close to the milestone on several occasions.Babar’s latest failure comes as Pakistan attempt to stay alive in a Test where England have been firmly in control.Yousuf takes aim at coachesFormer Pakistan cricketer and batting coach Mohammad Yousuf has previously expressed concerns over Babar’s technical shortcomings and has now criticised the coaches around the star batter for failing to address those issues."A few years ago I warned about this, but unfortunately some so-called coaches around Babar Azam & other players didn’t allow him to work on issues that could have been easily resolved. That failure has dragged Pakistan cricket into the decline we see today," he wrote in a caption while sharing the video on X.Yousuf went on to launch a stronger attack on the coaching setup, claiming that poor guidance has hindered the development of Pakistan’s talented players."These coaches are poison for the game. They lack vision, they block progress, and they misguide even the most talented players. If our cricketers don’t learn who to listen to, their careers will end far sooner than they should. The poor technique of our players has now been brutally exposed from Bangladesh to England. What could have been corrected years ago has instead become a glaring weakness, leaving Pakistan cricket vulnerable and struggling on the international stage," he added.The team’s poor overseas record has added to the pressure, with Pakistan losing nine of their last 10 matches away from home, their only victory in that run coming against the West Indies.Babar’s individual struggles have also coincided with considerable changes in Pakistan’s leadership. articles.title: Auqib Nabi signs short-term County Championship deal ahead of New Zealand Test series
articles.summary: Cricket News: Jammu and Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi has secured a short-term deal with Surrey and will feature in three County Championship Division One matches as he .
articles.body: Jammu and Kashmir pacer Auqib Nabi has secured a short-term deal with Surrey and will feature in three County Championship Division One matches as he looks to sharpen his red-ball game ahead of India’s upcoming tour of New Zealand.According to cricinfo, Nabi received his UK work visa clearance on Saturday and travelled to England soon after. He is expected to make his Surrey debut against Yorkshire at The Oval on September 2.Move aimed at New Zealand preparationThe stint has been arranged with an eye on India’s two-Test tour of New Zealand in November. The BCCI is understood to have facilitated the move to give Nabi valuable experience in English conditions, where seam movement and red-ball bowling can provide useful preparation for the New Zealand assignment.Nabi’s stock has risen significantly in recent months. He was recently called into India’s Test squad as a replacement for injured pace spearhead Jasprit Bumrah for the Sri Lanka series, although he did not get a game after India opted for Prasidh Krishna and Mohammed Siraj.Stellar Ranji Trophy campaignThe 29-year-old was one of the standout performers in Jammu and Kashmir’s historic maiden Ranji Trophy title-winning campaign.Nabi finished the 2025-26 tournament as the leading wicket-taker, claiming 60 wickets in 10 matches and 17 innings at an outstanding average of 12.56. His tally included seven five-wicket hauls, playing a major role in J&K’s breakthrough domestic triumph. He also represented India A on their recent tour of Sri Lanka, taking six wickets across two first-class matches.After his domestic heroics, he was bought by Delhi Capitals for Rs 8.4 crore in the 2026 IPL auction, featuring in five games but failing to pick up any wickets, leaking runs at an economy of 11.46.Surrey has had several Indian players wearing its colours, with Sai Sudharsan having short stints in 2023 and 2024 and then Rajasthan batter Mahipal Lomror being signed for six matches earlier this month. articles.title: Imran Khan row: PCB warns Pakistan players against speaking about jailed former captain
articles.summary: Cricket News: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has advised players involved in the ongoing Test series against England to refrain from making public comments about .
articles.body: The Pakistan Cricket Board (PCB) has advised players involved in the ongoing Test series against England to refrain from making public comments about the imprisonment and health of former Pakistan captain Imran Khan, according to a report by PTI.The development comes amid growing international attention on Imran's continued incarceration and concerns over his reported health condition. The issue came into sharper focus during the second Test at Lord's after Sky Sports aired an interview with Imran's sons, Suleman and Kasim Khan, during the lunch interval.According to PTI, the PCB was unhappy with the interview and considered it political in nature. However, the board decided against prolonging the dispute, with Pakistan also scheduled to attend a reception hosted by Prince Charles on September 2 and mindful of the country's diplomatic relations with the United Kingdom.PCB wary of players being drawn into Imran debatePakistan head coach Sarfaraz Ahmed was asked during a media interaction whether the players had watched the interview with Imran's sons conducted by former England batter Mike Atherton.Sarfaraz said the players were unaware of it as they were having lunch."No we don't know anything about it, we were having lunch," he said when asked about the interview and reports that the PCB had threatened not to send the players back onto the field after lunch if the interview was broadcast.PTI reported that the PCB subsequently advised members of the playing group not to comment on Imran's imprisonment. The move comes as international media attention around the former Pakistan captain has intensified, with several former cricketers and prominent figures voicing concerns over his reported health and access to medical treatment.Imran, 73, has been imprisoned at Adiala Jail in Rawalpindi since 2023 after being convicted in corruption cases. He continues to deny the allegations.The political issue has increasingly intersected with the cricketing world because of Imran's status as Pakistan's 1992 World Cup-winning captain and one of the country's most celebrated cricketers.Moin Khan joins growing chorus of supportFormer Pakistan wicketkeeper-batter Moin Khan, a member of Imran's 1992 World Cup-winning side, recently made an emotional appeal for authorities to ensure that his former captain receives proper medical care.“Our captain Imran Khan, as you all know, is currently in Adiala jail, and his condition is quite bad at present. One more time, I will urge the authorities, the government of Pakistan and all those people who run the Adiala jail,” Moin said in a video message.“My request is that our captain’s right, as a former prime minister, as a citizen of Pakistan, his right to medical care should be honoured. Whatever he needs, it should be seen to,” he added.Moin also urged fellow cricketers to publicly express their support for Imran.“Besides, I also urge other cricketers to speak up and voice their support for him. Imran Khan’s contribution to Pakistan cricket [is immense] and all of us who played in his era learnt a lot from him. He has given Pakistan cricket a lot,” he said.His comments came shortly after former Pakistan captain Javed Miandad also made an impassioned appeal for Imran's release, describing his former teammate as an honest person.The concerns have extended beyond Pakistan, with 22 former international captains from countries including India, England, West Indies and New Zealand writing to Pakistan Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif seeking adequate medical care and constitutional safeguards for Imran.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: 1,300 days, 36 innings, no hundred: How Babar Azam’s Test century drought became a long-running story
articles.summary: Cricket News: For a batter who once seemed to make Test hundreds almost on demand, Babar Azam’s wait for another three-figure score has become remarkably long. Baba.
articles.body: For a batter who once seemed to make Test hundreds almost on demand, Babar Azam’s wait for another three-figure score has become remarkably long. Babar’s last Test century came on December 26, 2022, when he made a brilliant 161 against New Zealand in Karachi. That innings was his ninth Test hundred and capped a remarkable 2022 in which he scored 1,184 Test runs, including four centuries.Since then, the Pakistan captain has played 17 Tests and 36 innings without reaching 100. The drought has stretched through home series, overseas tours, changes in captaincy and a succession of scores that suggested a century was always around the corner, but never quite arrived.And the latest England series has added another chapter. It started immediately after the 161The century drought effectively began in the very next innings after Babar's 161. He was dismissed for 14 in the second innings of that New Zealand Test, before scoring 24 and 27 in the second Test in Karachi. The 2023 tour of Sri Lanka brought scores of 13, 24 and 39, while the subsequent tour of Australia produced 21, 14, 1, 41, 26 and 23 across three Tests.The 41 at Melbourne was his highest Test score of the period at the time, but it was another innings that ended before he could build a substantial score.2024: The drought turns into a crisisBabar's struggles became even more pronounced in 2024. Against Bangladesh, he managed 0, 22, 31 and 11 across the two Tests. Then came the home series against England, where he made only 30 in the first Test at Multan. He was dismissed LBW by Chris Woakes on a pitch where Shan Masood and Abdullah Shafique both scored centuries.That 30 extended his run of innings without even a Test fifty. His fortunes finally changed in South Africa at the end of the year. Babar scored 50 in the first Test at Centurion, his first Test fifty since the 161 against New Zealand, before going one better in the second Test at Cape Town.There, he made 58 in the first innings and 81 in the second, falling 19 runs short of what would have been his 10th Test century.2025: Getting close, but never close enoughBabar began 2025 with that 81 against South Africa as one of the highlights of the year. Across the two-Test series, he accumulated 193 runs, with a best of 81 and three fifties, but still no century. The pattern continued through the rest of the year. His calendar-year Test numbers were considerably better than in 2023 and 2024, but the hundred remained elusive. His best score in 2025 was 81.2026: The biggest missed chance - 88 against West IndiesIn the second Test at Port of Spain, Babar made 88, putting himself just 12 runs away from the milestone. He was eventually run out by Brandon King after a mix-up, ending another promising attempt at his 10th Test century. Earlier in the series, he had also made 58 not out in the first Test chase, but Pakistan lost by 90 runs.Babar's 193 runs in the two-Test West Indies series, including the 88 and an unbeaten 24, briefly lifted him back into the ICC Test top 10. Yet the century still refused to come.Bangladesh offered another openingBefore the England tour, Babar also scored 68 and 47 in the two-Test series against Bangladesh. The 68 was another useful contribution, but once again he failed to turn a start into the hundred that has been missing from his Test record for nearly four years.England: Injury, comeback and another failureBabar missed the first Test against England at Headingley after suffering a finger injury. Pakistan went on to lose by an innings and 103 runs. He returned for the second Test at Lord's after declaring himself 90 per cent fit.But the comeback has so far failed to provide the response Pakistan wanted. In Pakistan's first innings at Lord's, Babar was dismissed for 8, caught by Jordan Cox off Josh Tongue as Pakistan collapsed to 110 all out.Chasing 389 in the second innings, Pakistan again lost Babar early. Jofra Archer's pace and bounce forced an awkward shot, with the ball ballooning to Jordan Cox at third slip. Babar departed for just 6.Two innings. Two low scores. Still no century.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: King Charles: Pakistan to meet King following controversial Lord's Test
articles.summary: Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.
articles.body:
Pakistan will have an audience with King Charles this week, days after a threat to cancel their tour of England was made because of an interview with the sons of Imran Khan.

During lunch on day one of the second Test, Sky Sports aired an interview with Suleiman and Kasim Khan, the sons of former Pakistan captain and prime minister Imran.

Imran Khan has been in prison for the past three years on charges of corruption, which he denies.

Before the interview was aired, the Pakistan Cricket Board raised the prospect of not resuming the second Test at Lord's and cancelling the remainder of the three-match series.

At the time, the England and Wales Cricket Board took government advice from the Foreign, Commonwealth and Development Office.

Buckingham Palace has confirmed the King is expected to meet the tourists later this week in an engagement planned before the series began.

"His Majesty the King, as Head of the Commonwealth, will receive the Pakistan Men's Test Cricket Team for an audience in the gardens of Clarence House, in the break between the second and third Test matches hosted in England over the summer," said a statement.

It is understood His Majesty will spend around 15 minutes with the Pakistan team.

Legendary all-rounder Imran Khan, 73, had a 21-year international career for Pakistan and famously led his team to World Cup glory in 1992.

He served as Pakistan's prime minister from 2018 to 2022 and was jailed a year later.

Sarfaraz denies knowing about Pakistan threat to end tour

In December of last year, Imran Khan's sister appealed to King Charles in his position of head of the Commonwealth to speak out on the situation.

According to The Times, Aleema Khanum said: "Pakistan is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations.

"Its key principles in the charter are rule of law, democracy, and human rights. A member nation is busy destroying all three fundamental principles.

"Member states, especially where King Charles is the head of the Commonwealth organisation, don't speak out against fascism or military dictatorship? What is the point of just organisations then?"

The chairman of the PCB, Mohsin Naqvi, serves as interior minister for the current Pakistan government. The PCB has been contacted for confirmation Naqvi will be present for the audience with the King.

Before the interview with Khan's sons aired, Sky received a complaint, yet pressed ahead with airing a version of former England captain Michael Atherton's conversation with Suleiman and Kasim.

In the interview, Suleiman and Kasim expressed concerns over the treatment and security given to their father, as well as criticising the UK government's response.

Despite the controversy caused by the interview, the Pakistan team returned to the field as scheduled after lunch on the opening day of the second Test.

At the close of play on the second day, Pakistan coach Sarfaraz Ahmed said he and his team did not know about the interview.

"I don't know anything. I'm just focusing on the match," said Sarfaraz. "You're talking about the interview? We don't know about the interview."

Speaking to BBC Sport at the conclusion of the second Test, Pakistan captain Babar Azam denied there was ever the threat of not playing, describing the story as "rumours".

In October, England will tour Pakistan for a one-day tri-series against the home side and Sri Lanka.

It will be England's fourth separate tour of Pakistan in the past four years following a 17-year gap between visits to the country because of security concerns.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: Deepti Sharma reached another landmark in her distinguished international career on Sunday, becoming only the third Indian player to feature in 150 women’s T20Is. The experienced all-rounder achieved the milestone during India’s Women’s T20 Asia Cup 2026 Group A opener against Thailand in Dubai, joining captain Harmanpreet Kaur and Smriti Mandhana in an exclusive Indian club.Harmanpreet leads the list with 202 T20I appearances, while Mandhana has played 171. Deepti also became only the 12th woman cricketer overall to reach the 150-match mark in the shortest format.The milestone is another reflection of Deepti’s longevity and importance to India. Before Sunday’s match, she had scored 1,270 runs and taken 168 wickets in 149 T20Is since making her international debut more than a decade ago.Deepti’s decade of impactDeepti has established herself as one of the most valuable all-rounders in the Indian setup, capable of changing the course of a match with either bat or ball. Her ability to bowl important overs, contribute runs in the middle and lower order and handle pressure situations has made her a key part of India’s plans across major tournaments.Her record in the Women’s Asia Cup further underlines her impact in the competition. Sunday’s game was her fourth edition of the tournament after making her debut in 2018. She came into the match with 19 Asia Cup appearances, 148 runs and 26 wickets.Her highest score in the tournament is 64, which came against the UAE in 2022, while her best bowling figures are 3/7 against Thailand in the same edition. Deepti has been particularly effective with the ball, finishing as the leading wicket-taker in each of the previous two editions.In 2022, she claimed 13 wickets to finish at the top of the bowling charts, edging Sri Lanka’s Inoka Ranaweera, who also took 13 wickets, on the basis of her superior economy rate and bowling average. Deepti retained the leading-wicket-taker tag in 2024 after taking 10 wickets.With Dubai conditions potentially offering assistance to spinners, her experience could again prove crucial for India as they look to make a strong start to their campaign.Pratika Rawal handed maiden T20I capThe Thailand game also marked an important moment for Pratika Rawal, who received her maiden T20I cap from Harmanpreet. Rawal was brought into the squad after Jemimah Rodrigues was ruled out of the Asia Cup and the upcoming Asian Games with a right hamstring injury.Harmanpreet confirmed before the match that Rawal would make her debut and said India wanted to play with greater ruthlessness during the tournament.“Today Pratika is making her debut because Jemi is not there. Playing good cricket is what we want to do. We have spoken about being ruthless and this is an important tournament for us,” Harmanpreet said.India entered the Asia Cup looking to overcome an inconsistent run in T20Is, having lost nine of their previous 16 matches this year. Thailand won the toss and opted to field, with captain Thipatcha Putthawong saying her side was excited to face India and hoping to restrict them to no more than 170.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Joe Root’s side seal series victory in second Test at Lord’s as ruthless Ollie Robinson shines again
articles.summary: England surged to a 194-run victory against Pakistan in the second Test of their three-match series at Lord's; watch England's third Test against Pakistan live on Sky Sports Cricket on Thursday, September 10
articles.body:
On a pitch that was heavily weighted towards the bowlers, England advanced their lead by 32 runs on day four to set Pakistan a huge total of 389 to win.

Mohammad Abbas tore through England's tail order on Sunday, taking a haul of five wickets, as the hosts were bowled out for 208 runs.

Pakistan were unable to surpass the hosts' lead, with a ruthless Ollie Robinson, back at his happy hunting ground at Lord's, taking four wickets on Sunday to bring up a match haul of eight as the hosts rattled their way through the visitors' batting line-up.

"I think the guys have shown great adaptability," Root said. "We've overcome some difficult situations when we were at 80-4 to get the total that we did.

"We showed great maturity and an element of problem-solving. It doesn't always have to be the top order that gets you runs.

"I thought the way the guys played towards the back end was excellent. If our tailenders can eke out 50 to 80 runs, that can be the difference in a Test match.

"I think the way we went about it with the bat, in very tough conditions, has been outstanding."

While it had seemed England would rattle their way to a comfortable victory on Sunday, Saud Shakeel (97) showed a lot of heart and made life difficult for England's bowlers, swiping away 13 fours and two booming sixes.

Agonisingly, as he attempted to slog the England bowlers, he pulled Josh Tongue out to the boundary at deep point, where Harry Brook was waiting to snaffle up the catch.

Pakistan were bowled out for 194 on Sunday, with Player of the Match, Robinson, taking the wickets of Pakistan's Azan Awais (7) and Abdullah Shafique (0) in the space of four deliveries, before also snaring Mohammad Rizwan (1) and Abdullah Shafique (0).

Jofra Archer also impressed, again showcasing his lightning pace to take figures of 2-73, while Josh Tongue returned 3-46.

Relentless Robinson stars again at Lord's

Robinson took seven wickets during England's defeat to New Zealand at Lord's in June, and outdid that total on Sunday at Lord's.

Rather remarkably, the Sussex bowler, who has won the Player of the Match award in all three of his three Test starts this summer, took remarkable match figures of 8-35 from 27 overs.

While it was much brighter at Lord's on day four, clouds continued to roll over The Home of Cricket, and Robinson still managed to extract plenty of movement out of the wicket, as he removed both Awais and Shafique in the same over.

"The way we've operated with the ball has been excellent," Root said. "We've got great contrast and variety in our attack.

"Obviously Ollie [Robinson] has been outstanding and is well complemented with three other 90mph bowlers that ask different questions."

Archer left Pakistan reeling at 3-14, playing a brutal bouncer to Babar, who swung wildly and edged the ball to Jordan Cox, waiting at third slip.

England then struggled before lunch. Shan Masood (26) and Shakeel dug deep to bring up a fourth-wicket partnership of 97 off 139 deliveries, before rain put a brief pause on proceedings.

The pair batted beautifully, with Shakeel smashing shots all around the ground, but as Pakistan reached 111 - or, more superstitiously, a Nelson - Robinson clattered the ball into his front pad. The umpire rejected England's appeals, prompting Root to review.

Hawk-Eye showed the ball hitting Masood's leg stump, and the umpire was overruled. It was the third time England had successfully challenged an umpire's decision off a Robinson delivery during the match.

Three overs later, Robinson had Rizwan (1) lbw, before Archer skittled Ali Usman (16).

Tongue would claim the final two wickets, bowling Khurram Shahzad (9) and Mohammad Ali (8), as England sealed victory.

Imam-ul-Haq would not turn out to bat due to a calf injury.

Abbas gets his name on Lord's honours board

After striking a superb half-century on day three, Dan Lawrence (54) returned to the crease alongside Ollie Robinson (8), but both were soon sent walking within six overs by Abbas.

On day three, Abbas dismissed both of Emilio Gay (31), Harry Brook (34) and Jamie Smith (7), and he got straight back to work on day four, taking out Lawrence's leg stump with a beautiful nip-back delivery, after the England batter had brought up his second half-century in as many games on Saturday.

Noting how much Abbas was getting the ball to jag, Rizwan once again stood up to the stumps and it paid off, with Robinson walking next with England 187-9 after 51.1 overs.

The England bowler, pinned back in his crease, edged Abbas behind to Rizwan, after the Pakistan bowler nipped a ball back to his off stump.

After securing his fifth wicket, Abbas dropped to the ground, overcome with emotion as he celebrated his milestone.

Pakistan's fielding has been called into question multiple times during the first two matches of this series, but their captain, Babar, set the standard on Sunday morning, producing a sensational direct hit from the covers to remove Josh Tongue (12).

articles.title: Cricket: Ballyspallen forced to concede match over broken printer
articles.summary: A team has been forced to concede a match in Northern Ireland because of a broken printer.
articles.body:
A team has been forced to concede a match in Northern Ireland because of a broken printer.

Ballyspallen were hosting Eglinton in the North West Cricket Union Premier League on Saturday.

Eglinton were all out for 159 in 48.1 overs and the hosts were on 19, just two overs into their response, when rain hit at Ballyspallen.

Overs were set to be lost and officials declared that the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern (DLS) method was to be calculated.

However, a broken printer meant that a DLS sheet could not be produced and, as a result, the visiting Eglinton team were awarded the victory without a further ball being bowled.

North West Cricket Union regulations state the team which hosts the match will immediately concede the game if a DLS sheet cannot be produced to both sides and umpires.

The regulations also state that the home club should have "a computer loaded with the necessary software, a compatible and operational printer with a sufficient supply of paper and ink, and a proficient operator".

The NWCU adds that it should be "operational" prior to the start of the match, but Ballyspallen's technical hiccup denied them a chance of a fifth win in the Premier League and they remain rooted to the bottom of the table.

articles.body: Ollie Robinson has produced a remarkable statistical landmark in Test cricket, moving past Jasprit Bumrah to claim the best bowling average among bowlers with at least 20 Tests over the last 100 years.Robinson reached the mark during England’s second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s on Sunday, as his four-wicket burst helped put England firmly in control of the fourth innings. The England seamer entered the day already among the most efficient Test bowlers of the modern era and strengthened his numbers further by dismantling Pakistan’s resistance.With his wickets in the second innings, Robinson’s career average moved to around 19.5, taking him past Bumrah’s previous benchmark of 19.79 for bowlers who made their Test debuts after 2000 and have played at least 20 matches.At the time of this report, Robinson had played 23 Tests, bowling in 43 innings and taking 99 wickets at an average of 19.53. His best innings figures are 5/39.Bumrah, meanwhile, has taken 234 wickets in 52 Tests at an average of 19.79, with best figures of 6/27.Best Test Bowling Average (Min. 20 Tests)W Barnes (England - 1890): 21 Tests, 51 wickets, Ave. 15.54, Best 6/28SF Barnes (England - 1914): 27 Tests, 189 wickets, Ave. 16.43, Best 9/103R Peel (England - 1896): 20 Tests, 101 wickets, Ave. 16.98, Best 7/31J Briggs (England - 1899): 33 Tests, 118 wickets, Ave. 17.75, Best 8/11OE Robinson* (England - 2026*): 23 Tests, 99 wickets, Ave. 19.53, Best 5/39JJ Bumrah (India - 2026*): 52 Tests, 234 wickets, Ave. 19.79, Best 6/27Robinson tears through Pakistan resistanceRobinson’s statistical achievement came while he was playing a pivotal role in England’s push for victory at Lord’s.Pakistan were 140/5 at tea on the fourth afternoon, chasing a daunting 389 after England had taken command of the second Test. Robinson broke a stubborn 97-run partnership between Saud Shakeel and Shan Masood, before quickly adding the wicket of Mohammad Rizwan.By tea, Robinson had figures of 4/24 in the innings and had taken eight wickets for 35 runs across the match.Shakeel had produced Pakistan’s strongest batting performance of the innings, reaching 78 to register his second half-century of the series. Masood, meanwhile, scored 26 as the pair frustrated England for almost four hours after Pakistan had slipped to 14/3.The partnership came after Robinson and Jofra Archer had initially threatened to run through Pakistan's middle order in seaming conditions.Four wickets put England within touching distanceRobinson returned with wicketkeeper Jamie Smith standing up to the stumps and immediately made the breakthrough. Masood was initially given not out after missing an inswinger, but England reviewed the decision and secured an lbw verdict with the ball striking him in line with leg stump.Robinson then removed Rizwan for one. The Pakistan batter attempted a swat but missed and was struck in front of the stumps.Shakeel had earlier reached his 15th Test half-century from 54 balls, using an attacking approach while Masood largely focused on occupying the crease. His 78 remained Pakistan's highest score of the innings and briefly raised hopes of an unlikely fightback.England's bowlers had become increasingly frustrated after lunch as Shakeel and Masood resisted for long periods, prompting repeated requests for the umpires to inspect the ball.But Robinson's return changed the momentum once again.His latest spell not only left England on the verge of victory in the second Test but also strengthened a statistical case that places him alongside some of the most effective Test bowlers of the modern era.With 99 wickets from 23 Tests and an average hovering around 19.5, Robinson is now just one wicket away from reaching three figures while sitting above Bumrah on the bowling-average list.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: England vs Pakistan: Ollie Robinson inspires series win despite Saud Shakeel defiance
articles.summary: England once again steamroller Pakistan to power to a series win on the fourth day of the second Test at Lord’s.
articles.body:
Second Rothesay Test, Lord's (day four of five)

England 290 (Smith 61, Cox 55; Abbas 4-73) & 208 (Lawrence 54; Abbas 5-57)

Pakistan 110 (Awais 46; Robinson 4-11) & 194 (Shakeel 97, Robinson 4-24)

England won by 194 runs, lead three-match series 2-0

England once again steamrollered Pakistan to power to a series win on the fourth day of the second Test at Lord's.

Despite being delayed by a defiant 97 by Saud Shakeel, England dismissed the tourists to win by 194 runs.

Ollie Robinson continued his sensational comeback summer, claiming 4-24 on Sunday for match figures of 8-35.

He expertly exploited the lavish movement on offer to conclude a similarly one-sided contest to England's innings win in the first Test at Headingley last week.

It means Joe Root has won the first two Tests of his second reign as captain, winning this series with a match to spare, in the process earning England's first series triumph since 2024.

Pakistan were set a Lord's record 389 to win, but a more realistic target was to drag the match into a fifth day – their previous highest total in the series was 171.

And when Robinson took two wickets in his third over to help reduce Pakistan to 14-3 it became apparent the Test would be completed inside four days – less than three days of cricket given the time lost to the weather.

Shakeel ensured the visitors were not routed, only for Robinson to return to remove Shan Masood and Muhammad Rizwan in successive overs.

When Shakeel holed out off Josh Tongue, any lingering doubts that England would not beat the fading light disappeared as Pakistan subsided to 194 all out.

The third and final Test of the series begins at Edgbaston on Wednesday, 9 September.

'14,000 runs for a reason' - Root calm on form

'His best Test for a year' - England-Pakistan player ratings

England seal series win over Pakistan - reaction & analysis

One-sided Test more eventful off the field than on

This Test may be remembered more for what happened off the field than anything that took place on it.

The build-up was dominated by the Brydon Carse controversy, then on the first day the Pakistan Cricket Board threatened to abandon the match and the rest of the tour over an interview broadcast by Sky with the sons of former captain and Prime Minister Imran Khan.

The action itself was almost a carbon copy of Headingley: Robinson continued his stellar return to Test cricket as leader of an England attack thrown together in the aftermath of Ben Stokes' retirement and showing huge signs of promise for the future.

In England's top six, Jordan Cox and Dan Lawrence again made half-centuries to hint they are worth persevering with, while opener Emilio Gay still needs a score to cement his place.

Bar some occasional uneven bounce, the Lord's pitch was much improved on the surface on which England beat New Zealand in June. The exaggerated assistance on offer to the seamers throughout was as much to do with the wet weather as the pitch.

In such conditions, Pakistan are always likely to struggle, just as England are often second-best against the turning ball when they go away from home.

Still, in these first two Tests, England have been as good as Pakistan have been poor. Surely a 3-0 clean sweep will be secured at Edgbaston.

Pakistan to meet King Charles after Lord's controversy

Robinson himself has admitted that he agreed with some of the reasoning as to why he was left out of the England team for more than two years under former captain Stokes and coach Brendon McCullum.

Naturally, there will be thoughts of what might have been for England had Robinson not been absent. Now he is back he is enjoying a remarkable summer – 23 wickets in three Tests at an average of eight.

He is the ideal bowler for a modern game when the moving ball is making batting a challenge. Operating with no great pace – Robinson often has the wicketkeeper standing up – the Sussex man relentlessly targets the stumps and pads with unerring accuracy and fingertip control.

Robinson has formed a contrasting and effective new-ball partnership with Jofra Archer, who once again bowled with high pace. Robinson had already prised out Azan Awais and Abdullah Shafique by the time Archer removed Pakistan captain Babar Azam with an 89mph bouncer.

A 23-over stand between Shakeel and Masood forced Root to try different plans – Lawrence bowled two overs of his off-spin – until the skipper once again summoned the reliable Robinson.

Masood was lbw on review, and Rizwan was leg before having a swipe. Archer and Tongue wrapped up the tail, meaning Robinson did not return for a shot at a five-wicket haul.

This was the day Pakistan lost the series yet, bizarrely, it may also have been their best performance thanks to the efforts of Muhammad Abbas and Shakeel.

The skilful Abbas had narrowly missed out on the Lord's honours board on three previous occasions and the 36-year-old made no mistake after England resumed on 177-7. Lawrence was bowled by a nip-backer and Robinson edged behind to give Abbas 5-57, which he celebrated with a point to the sky.

Three wickets down inside 7.1 overs and with Imam-ul-Haq absent injured, Pakistan could have been humiliated had it not been for Shakeel.

First in the partnership of 97 with Masood, Shakeel showed the patience and technique to resist the England attack. The left-hander was brave, too, coming through blows to the helmet from Archer and Tongue.

When Tongue went to a sustained bouncer plan, Shakeel swiped successive sixes, then a pull for four to move to 96. In the same over, he tried another pull that dropped looped between two England fielders on the off side.

The plan did not change for Tongue's next over. Shakeel set himself for the blow that would have brought up his century, only to find Harry Brook on the long leg boundary.

Tongue ended with 3-46, Archer 2-73. In four innings in this series, Pakistan have not reached 200.

articles.title: England vs Pakistan player ratings: Ollie Robinson stars again but is Joe Root's form a worry?
articles.summary: Who produced their best Test performance in 12 months? Which batter is building a case to test the selectors? Player ratings from England's win over Pakistan.
articles.body:
England have a series victory for the first time since 2024 after outclassing Pakistan again in a 194-run victory in the second Test.

Ben Duckett - 4 - Another quiet Test for Duckett whose total of 18 runs across the match was only three more than at Headingley last week. Could do little about his first-innings dismissal but the way he hit a drive straight to mid-off in the second was really poor.

Emilio Gay - 5 - So unlucky to be the latest victim of the poor Lord's pitch after reaching 31 in the second innings. The third Test at Edgbaston could be a big week for the opener.

Jordan Cox - 7 - Very impressive again in making 55 in the first innings. As wickets fell around him, Cox remained composed. Yet to make a score that completely forces the selectors' hand but he is building a strong case to stay when Jacob Bethell is fit again.

Joe Root - 5 - Scores of four and 24 as England's captain fell lbw in both innings. Seven of his nine Test dismissals this summer have been in that fashion. It is not a crisis... yet…

Harry Brook - 6 - Nothing spectacular from Brook, who made 15 and 34, but he took a more restrained approach than in similar recent Tests when faced with difficult conditions.

Dan Lawrence - 7 - After being dropped and then run out in making 17 in the first innings, Lawrence responded with a useful 54 in the second that suggested he does have the skills for this role, with the bat at least.

Jamie Smith - 8 - His best performance for a year. Smith's 61 in difficult conditions in the first innings was perfectly played. Again, kept well up to the stumps to Ollie Robinson. His glovework has gone up a level.

Gus Atkinson - 5 - The one member of England's pace quartet who is struggling for wickets. Bowled quickly on day four but still only has one scalp in the series. His 45 with the bat in the first innings was handy.

Ollie Robinson - 9 - This is turning into Ollie Robinson's summer. After another eight wickets, England's seamer now has 23 wickets in three Tests at an average of 8.34 since his recall.

Jofra Archer - 8 - Brilliant in the first innings when he was unfortunate to finish with just the three wickets. His bouncer to dismiss Babar Azam on day four was a throwback of Archer's fearsome debut on the same ground.

Josh Tongue - 7 - Pakistan did not recover after Tongue took the key wickets of Babar Azam and Abdullah Shafique in the first innings. Also improved his Test high score to 30 not out.

Shan Masood - 5 - Battled in the second innings for 26 but only made one in the first.

Azan Awais - 6 - Rode his luck against Archer but otherwise played nicely for 46 in the first innings before being Robinson'd in the second.

Abdullah Shafique - 2 - Five in the first innings, a duck in the second. Shafique was Pakistan's best batter in the first Test but went missing here.

Imam-ul-Haq - 1 - Didn't bat, didn't bowl, dropped a catch.

Babar Azam - 2 - Best thing he did was win the toss.

Saud Shakeel - 7- Finally a bit of fight from Pakistan. Deserved his century.

Muhammad Rizwan - 5 - A mark boosted by his admirable keeping up to the stumps.

Ali Usman - 4 - These were not conditions for a spinner so hard to judge fairly. He is not a Test number eight with the bat, never mind seven where he had to emerge here after Imam's injury.

Khurram Shahzad - 3 - Just as expensive as Headingley and only took three wickets despite favourable conditions.

Muhammad Abbas - 8 - Nine wickets in the match, including 5-57 in the second innings to put him on the honours board. Much improved on Headingley and a constant threat with conditions in his favour.

Mohammad Ali - 6 - Also better than he was at Headingley, nipping the ball in and out, but he won't find conditions better suited to his style.

articles.title: ENG vs PAK 2nd Test: England thrash Pakistan by 194 runs at Lord’s to take an unassailable 2-0 series lead
articles.summary: Cricket News: England completed an emphatic 194-run victory over Pakistan at Lord’s on Sunday, wrapping up the second Test inside four days to take an unassailable .
articles.body: England completed an emphatic 194-run victory over Pakistan at Lord’s on Sunday, wrapping up the second Test inside four days to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the three-match series. The result also ended England’s wait for a Test series victory, with their previous series win coming in December 2024.Set a daunting 389 for victory, Pakistan were bowled out for 194 around 45 minutes after tea, continuing a miserable batting campaign in which they have failed to reach 200 even once in the series. England needed only 18 wickets to win the Test after Pakistan opener Imam-ul-Haq was ruled out of the remainder of the match after tearing his left calf on the opening day.The third and final Test will be played in Birmingham from September 9, but the series result is already beyond Pakistan’s reach.Robinson, Archer and Tongue break PakistanOllie Robinson was the standout performer for England, producing another superb spell of seam bowling to finish with eight wickets in the match. He took 4/24 on Sunday and ended with remarkable match figures of 8/35, repeatedly troubling Pakistan's batters with his control and movement.Jofra Archer (2/73) also played a key role, combining his raw pace with Robinson's skill and making an important contribution to Pakistan's collapse. Josh Tongue completed the demolition job with three wickets as England cleaned up the tail.Pakistan had begun the fourth day at 14/3 and needed something extraordinary to stay alive in the chase. Saud Shakeel provided it for a while, producing the most substantial innings by a Pakistan batter in the series.Shakeel and Shan Masood put together a stubborn 97-run partnership that frustrated England for almost four hours. Shakeel eventually fell for 97, caught on the boundary while attempting to reach his century, ending the highest individual score by either side in the series.Shakeel's resistance not enoughShakeel had taken the attack to England after lunch, reaching his half-century from 54 balls before continuing to counterattack against the pace attack. He appeared increasingly comfortable against the short ball and began taking risks with the tailenders for company.Masood, who scored 26, concentrated on occupying the crease during their partnership, while Shakeel provided most of the attacking strokes. Their resistance finally ended when Robinson returned with wicketkeeper Jamie Smith standing up to the stumps.Masood was initially given not out after missing an inswinger, but England reviewed the decision and secured the lbw verdict. Robinson then removed Mohammad Rizwan for one to claim his 99th Test wicket before Josh Tongue and the rest of the attack finished the innings.Shakeel's dismissal for 97 summed up Pakistan's batting problems: he had shown the application and skill required to resist England, but there was virtually no support around him.With Imam unable to bat again, Pakistan's hopes disappeared completely. England's bowlers needed little time to wrap up the tail, triggering celebrations and handshakes at Lord's.The victory gives England an unassailable series lead with one Test still to play, while Pakistan must now regroup before the final match in Birmingham on September 9. articles.title: Joe Root: England captain calm on form, saying 'I've got 14,000 runs for a reason'
articles.summary: England captain Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his recent modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".
articles.body:
Joe Root is "not too concerned" about his recent modest returns with the bat, saying he has "14,000 runs for a reason".

Captain Root, England's all-time leading Test run-scorer, has passed 50 only twice this summer. An average of 29.44 is his second-lowest in a home season in a 14-year international career.

The 35-year-old has been lbw nine times in his past seven Tests, including on seven occasions this summer.

But Root pointed to the challenge faced by all batters against the moving ball in the UK this summer and his own remarkable Test career. Only India great Sachin Tendulkar has more than the Yorkshireman's 14,208 runs.

"I've played this game a long time and I've always found ways of solving those problems and working it through," Root told the BBC's Today at the Test. "I don't see this as being any different.

"There's a reason why I've got 14,000 runs and a reason why I've played the best part of 15 years at this level.

"Of course it's frustrating that there's sort of a trend. There are probably four umpires' calls within that, which could have gone the other way, and the ball is probably deviating more than it ever has.

"You try and be realistic and understand where everything's at, but also be aware of what you need to do to keep improving and keep getting better. I'm pretty sure I'll get through the other side. I'm not too concerned about that."

Last summer, former Australia opener David Warner took a dig at Root's prospects of success in the Ashes series that was to follow when he said: "He will have to take the surfboard off his front leg."

At the time, Warner's suggestion Root had an lbw problem was incorrect. In a run that began in August 2022 and ended with the fourth Ashes Test in Melbourne in December, Root was lbw to seam bowlers in Test cricket on only three occasions.

However, Root's recent run of leg-before dismissals began when he was trapped by Australia's Jhye Richardson in the second innings of the Boxing Day Test. Since then he has been lbw nine times in 12 innings, all to pace bowlers.

Root's specific problem has been against right-arm bowlers, pitching the ball outside off stump and nipping it back towards him.

Of the nine dismissals in his run of lbws, none have come at the hands of bowlers with high pace, rather those with a maximum speed of around 84mph.

"You're never given anything in this game," said Root. "You have to work for everything. You have to keep working hard and I'll certainly keep doing that.

"You're constantly going to get challenged and you're constantly going to have to look to evolve and learn, but that's never been something I've shied away from and I certainly won't be doing moving forward."

Root not only highlighted the difficulty of conditions, but also suggested batting is being made harder by what he perceived to be a different technique employed by ball manufacturers Dukes.

"The balls have been different this summer," he said. "I think there is a different lacquer. They were worried about it going out of shape. They are denting surfaces more."

When contacted by the BBC, Dukes denied any alteration to its process.

Root was backed to solve the lbw issue by former England captain Michael Vaughan, who said: "He's always overcome problems and I'm pretty sure he'll overcome this one.

"It is an issue because it's happening on a regular basis, but he's had issues in the past that he's managed to come back from. There's no question he'll be fine in time."

Despite there being no big contribution from the captain, England secured a series win over Pakistan with a 194-run win in the second Test at Lord's.

It gave Root a second win in as many matches at the beginning of his second spell as skipper, and England their first series victory since 2024.

The build-up to the second Test was dominated by the controversy surrounding England pace bowler Brydon Carse, who was dropped from the squad because of an incident outside a nightclub in Derby.

On Tuesday, Root said he was "hacked off" to be dealing with another drinking issue involving an England player and confirmed he had addressed his squad to warn them against a repeat.

On Sunday, Root said he wanted his players to celebrate the win at Lord's "sensibly".

"It's important that we're not talking about that, absolutely," said Root. "It's hard to win Test matches, it's hard to win Test series.

"Enjoy it and celebrate it, but in a sensible and grown-up way."

Vaughan suggested the England squad should "stay in".

"Have a quiet one," Vaughan said. "I don't want to be picking up the paper tomorrow morning or mid-afternoon on social media and seeing a few clicks. You've won a good series, just have a quiet night."

articles.title: Nasser Hussain says any side in world cricket would struggle against England bowling attack in current conditions
articles.summary: England's four-pronged pace attack has skittled Pakistan for under 200 four innings in a row with Ollie Robinson taking 16 wickets in two games at an average below eight and a fit and firing Jofra Archer bowling his quickest opening spell in Tests; England hold unassailable 2-0 lead
articles.body:
An inexperienced Pakistan outfit have been skittled for under 200 in all four innings so far, only batting in excess of 50 overs once, with the relentless accuracy of Ollie Robinson complemented superbly by the pace of Jofra Archer, Josh Tongue and Gus Atkinson.

Thoughts have inevitably turned to how the quartet may fare in the home Ashes next summer, a series England will be looking to win for the first time in over a decade, while there is also a mouth-watering assignment in South Africa in prospect this winter.

Speaking after Root's men rolled Pakistan for 194 on day four at Lord's to take an unassailable 2-0 lead in the thee-match contest, Sky Sports pundit Hussain said: "That four-pronged attack looks really strong, offering so many different things.

"I wouldn't judge them on how they go against Pakistan but I think pretty much any side in world cricket would find it hard work against this attack, in these conditions."

Robinson impresses - but more questions to come

The metronomic Robinson has led the way with 16 wickets across the first two Tests at an average of just 7.18, and when you add in his seven-wicket match haul against New Zealand at Lord's in June, his record for the summer is a remarkable 23 scalps at 8.34.

The 32-year-old had spent over two years in the international wilderness before his recent recall, mainly due to fitness concerns, but his return has been a raging success and highlighted just what England were missing during their Ashes drubbing last winter.

Hussain said of Robinson: "England bowled in some very useful conditions in The Ashes and kept dishing up short and wide deliveries - Travis Head could not believe the amount of cut shots he got away.

"It's been nice these last few months to see an England opening bowler using the skills he has to target the stumps and the pads, making sure he is always in the game. That's what Robinson does from the first ball to his last.

"There will be more questions asked of him, on difficult pitches to bowl seam on - his fitness will have to come into play. But in these conditions, he's England's best bowler - as good as you get

"For someone who was left out of the side for quite some time to suddenly come back and be England's best bowler is some achievement. You have to take your hat off to him.

"He now has to ask himself, the backroom staff, and people like Stuart Broad and James Anderson, 'what do I need to do to become the complete bowler?' That's how you grow as a player and a team."

Hussain: Archer has looked fit all summer

Archer, who has deserved more than the eight wickets he has picked up in the series so far, bowled his fastest opening spell in Test cricket when he clocked an average of 90.7mph against Pakistan in the Lord's Test, according to CricViz .

Hussain added: "I spoke to Archer here during the ODI series against India this summer and he said 'I am consistently bowling well' - and not in an arrogant way.

"Everyone has also noted how fit Jofra has looked all summer.

"People were worried when he came back from the IPL whether he had got enough overs and workload in and he was left out of the first Test against New Zealand. But has played a lot of cricket since, playing all the time.

"Stuart Broad made the excellent point that when he worries about fitness, speeds and rhythm is when bowlers play and then don't play again for a month. Jofra playing all the time means he can sustain his speeds."

Broad has also been enthused by England's attack and feels there is no need to break it up by introducing a frontline spinner - but he warned the bowler-friendly conditions means only so much can be gleaned from their success.

The Sky Cricket expert added: "Robinson has hit immaculate areas and moved the ball consistently. The other seamers hit 90mph consistently, so you have variety.

"My belief is that we don't have a good enough spinner so why bother when you have South Africa away and the Ashes next summer?

"Root will be delighted with what he has seen but what will frustrate him slightly is how much the ball has been doing.

"I don't think we are learning a huge amount about the bowling unit or batting unit as it has been such different conditions.

"You don't see Test match batters get bowled or lbw as much as we have seen this summer and that is due to conditions.

"I don't know if we will end the summer going, 'we have learnt so much about this team, we are positive about what's coming in the future', but two wins out of two is exactly what you'd expect and the team have delivered."
